premise: The humble beginnings of a Delta blues legend who played on street corners before recording hits.
hook: He worked as a tractor driver in Mississippi cotton fields while earning coins by singing gospel and blues on street corners.
key_facts: Worked on a cotton plantation in Indianola, Mississippi, during his youth.
Traveled to Memphis, Tennessee, seeking a radio break, eventually working as a disc jockey known as the Beale Street Blues Boy.
Named his signature Gibson electric guitars 'Lucille' after an incident involving a tavern fire.
Recorded dozens of influential blues standards over a decades-long touring career.

premise: A young football player cut from the Canadian Football League finds himself with seven dollars and no backup plan.
hook: He had seven dollars in his pocket after his sports dream ended. Then he stepped into a wrestling ring.
key_facts: Played college football for the University of Miami national championship team
Cut from the Calgary Stampeders in the CFL early in his professional career
Transitioned to professional wrestling under the name Rocky Maivia before achieving global fame
Became one of the highest-paid actors in Hollywood

premise: A college dropout builds a computer in his parents' garage with his friend during the 1970s tech boom.
hook: Before building iPhones, he dropped out of college, slept on friends' floors, and built circuit boards in a garage.
key_facts: Dropped out of Reed College after attending for one semester
Co-founded Apple Computer in 1976 inside a suburban garage
Traveled to India seeking spiritual guidance prior to starting Apple

premise: A struggling single mother writes fantasy chapters in Edinburgh cafes while depending on state benefits.
hook: Before selling millions of books, she wrote manuscript pages in local cafes while keeping warm with her baby.
key_facts: Conceived the idea for a wizarding school while on a delayed train in 1990.
Completed the first novel while living in Edinburgh amid financial hardship.
Faced multiple rejections from publishing houses before Bloomsbury accepted the manuscript.

premise: How cutting the feet off her pantyhose led to founding Spanx.
hook: She had $5,000 in savings, zero fashion experience, and a pair of scissors.
key_facts: Worked as a door-to-door fax machine salesperson for seven years.
Cut the feet out of her control-top pantyhose to wear under white pants for a party.
Wrote her own patent application to save legal fees before launching the shapewear brand.

premise: His grueling decade training at the China Drama Academy as a child.
hook: Before he broke box office records, he trained for 19 hours a day under a master who promised teachers could break their bones.
key_facts: Enrolled in the Beijing Opera School (China Drama Academy) at age six by his parents.
Trained rigorously in martial arts, acrobatics, singing, and acting for ten years.
Worked as a stuntman and extra in Bruce Lee films before landing leading roles.

premise: Using his company's last remaining funds to play blackjack in Las Vegas after nearly going bankrupt.
hook: When FedEx was on the brink of collapse with $5,000 left, the founder flew to Vegas and gambled it.
key_facts: Founded Federal Express in 1971, facing massive startup costs and regulatory hurdles.
Used the remaining $5,000 of company funds to play blackjack and won $27,000.
The winnings kept the company's fuel tanks filled for a few more days until emergency funding arrived.

premise: Growing up in a small town in Haryana with a fascination for aviation before reaching space.
hook: She grew up in a town where girls rarely pursued engineering, yet sketched airplanes on her school notebooks every day.
key_facts: Graduated with a degree in Aeronautical Engineering from Punjab Engineering College in India.
Emigrated to the United States to earn master's and doctoral degrees in aerospace engineering.
Selected by NASA as an astronaut candidate in 1994, making her first spaceflight in 1997.

premise: Inventing a revolutionary tactile reading system for the blind after losing his sight as a young child.
hook: Blinded by an accident in his father's workshop at age three, he invented a code using six raised dots at age fifteen.
key_facts: Injured his right eye with a stitching awl in his father's harness-making shop, leading to total blindness.
Attended the Royal Institution for Blind Youth in Paris, where books were printed in heavy embossed raised letters.
Adapted a military 'night writing' code of raised dots to create the Braille alphabet.
